chapter_theme: ஞானம் - 4, a sixteen-stanza 'sutra' on பூரணம், the fullness that the elders called God: it is the sixteen kalas, kept by setting the mind at the suzhumunai and holding the vaasi, with the sun and moon breaths exchanged and gathered within the circle of the uvula, where body, life and fullness are one. Against this inner place the run sets the books, caste, idols of stone and copper, and the garbed beggars of 'mouth-knowledge', all invented so that the worldly might make a living; and it binds the disciple to secrecy and to living in accord with the world.
structure_note: Sixteen எண்சீர் விருத்தம் stanzas chaining by antadi throughout (ஆச்சே / ஆச்சப்பா; தானே / தானென்ற; பிழைக்கத்தானே / பிழைப்பதற்கு ... சொன்னேன் / பிரித்துரைத்தேன்). 2426 to 2430 define pooranam and attack the books, caste and idols; 2431 to 2434 give the practice at the suzhumunai in number-cipher (sixteen, eight, four, three, one); 2435 and 2436 are rules of conduct and a warning against garbed beggars; 2437 to 2439 locate pati in the body and list its names; 2440 and 2441 are the author's summary, which calls the run a sutra of twice eight stanzas, matching its sixteen units.

2426.reading: They said that pooranam is God, but one must say what pooranam is; I will tell the cause, listen with attention: the sixteen kalas are pooranam; in this death-dealing world, bewildered and witless, they scorned pooranam; if you set your mind on the elephant and guard pooranam, it becomes the Siva-yoga life called vaasi.
2426.nuance: The verse defines its own term: பூரணம் is the sixteen kalas, which tradition takes as the moon's digits matched to the breath, so that 'guarding pooranam' is keeping the breath whole. வாரணம் (elephant) is a cipher word, read by tradition as the breath or as Ganapati at the root centre; the verse gives no key. மாரணம் (killing) for the world is strong and may be a pun on மரணம்.

2427.reading: In this way the eighteen, Brahma, Vishnu, Hara and all the gods told us to know it as God, and the sages and rishis said the same; without talking, look at the book and keep the renowned pooranam in mind; those who guard pooranam live within the centre of the vaasi.
2427.nuance: பதினெண் பேரும் is the eighteen (gods, or the eighteen Siddhars, or the eighteen Puranas); the verse does not say. 'Look at the book' (நூலைப் பார்த்து) here means this book, in contrast to the many books attacked in 2428 to 2430. வாசி நடு மையம், the centre of the vaasi, is the central channel between the two breaths.

2428.reading: The great ones in the world who said 'I am that', after knowing pooranam the mother, drank the honey-nectar and did the silent Siva-yoga that never cloys; it was for those who trusted the body of flesh that the worldly set up 'the four Vedas', 'the six books', 'I', 'you' and 'caste', so that they might make a living.
2428.nuance: The verse makes caste, scripture and the I-you distinction one invention with one motive, livelihood (பிழைக்க), and the antadi carries பிழைக்க into 2429, where the argument is examined from the other side. பூரணம் is here தாய், the mother, which prepares the goddess-language of 2443 and 2448. தானென்ற பெரியோர்கள் are those who say 'I am that', the knowers of 2409.

2429.reading: 'If the many books were not said for a living, they would stay without knowing pooranam; if books were not tied on for them to toil at, they would wander witless in the world; caste, bindu, father, mother, child and wife were said for them to flourish and to toil, and there is no other way': so, noble one, the knowers sang.
2429.nuance: The verse gives the knowers' defence of the inventions of 2428: books, caste and family keep the unknowing from wandering witless. Whether Agasthiyar endorses the defence or reports it is left open; 2430 treats the result (fools who do not know the cipher) as a fact either way. உழைப்பதற்கு stands in both line 3 and line 7, and one may be a copyist's repetition.

2430.reading: If they had not sung and said it so, the fools of the world would not know the cipher; some, having looked at many books and forgotten themselves, attack others, fall into the pit and die; they waste away on 'name' and 'form', and take stone and copper in the world for God; the fools who seek without knowing pooranam will cease only by barking like dogs.
2430.nuance: பரிபாடை is the Siddhars' word for their cipher (பரிபாஷை), the coded language in which the books are written; the verse's point is that even the books are a cipher the fools cannot read. கற்செம்பைத் தெய்வமென்று, taking stone and copper for God, is the Siddhars' standard attack on idols, shared with Sivavakkiyar and Valmiki. நாய்போல குரைத்து, barking like dogs, is the disputation of 2413.

2431.reading: Those who wandered without seeing are crores upon crores, and those who knew the cause are crores upon crores; will one know it by wailing in vain, and what use is talking science? When without bending you set the mind at the suzhumunai, join the four to the guru's feet in the two-fours, and guard it shamelessly as one thought, the four and the eight become one: fix it and blow.
2431.nuance: The numbers are the run's cipher: tradition takes the four, the eight and the sixteen as the kalas of the breath (2432 maps them to life, pati's feet and pati), and ஊது (blow) as directing the breath. இருநான்கில் நாலைச் சேர்த்து (join the four to the two-fours) and குருபாதம் (the guru's feet, or the foot of the guru as a measure) are not explained. விஞ்ஞானம் here is discursive knowledge, not modern science.

2432.reading: He who knows the blowing of the one who blew is the siddha; noble one, the sixteen is pati, disputants, the two-fours are pati's feet, and the four kinds are life; seeing this path, the light and the full pooranam and these three, when you guard it there sleeping without sleeping, the Primal Parai and Hara become one within the circle of the uvula: see.
2432.nuance: This verse is the run's key to its own numbers: sixteen is pati, eight is pati's feet, four is life (உயிர்), and tradition matches these to the kalas of moon, sun and fire or to measures of the breath. அண்ணாக்கின் வட்டம், the circle of the uvula, is the place above the palate where Siddha yoga sets the union of Shakti and Siva (2433, 2438). தூங்காமற் றூங்கி, sleeping without sleeping, is the turiya state. வாதிகளே (disputants) as address is odd and may be corrupt.

2433.reading: Look: rising at dawn, without hurry set the mind at the suzhumunai; when the sun and moon exchange and rise at the suzhumunai that is the womb, standing within the uvula without wavering, see it subside within the suzhumunai; of the sixteen, the eight and the four and the three, without scattering, join as one and go.
2433.nuance: பரிதிமதி, the sun and moon, are the right and left breaths in the Siddhars' cipher, and their exchange at the central channel is the practice; a plain reading, that sunrise is the hour, is also present in உதயத்தில் எழுந்திருந்து. கருவான சுழுமுனை, the suzhumunai that is the womb or seed, repeats the run's link between the yogic centre and conception. The arithmetic of sixteen, eight, four and three is from 2432.

2434.reading: This alone is the one pooranam; this alone is what is called the risen kala; for those who have become clear, knowledge is siddhi; would knowledge come from what is said without fixing? Do not let loose in the open the knowledge the many primal gurus spoke; it becomes sin; it cannot be seen by those whose mind staggers; this is the secret told to the clear.
2434.nuance: The verse is the first of the run's three commands to secrecy (2434, 2438, 2441), and gives the reason: a staggering mind cannot see it, so saying it openly only makes sin. உகமை (secret, intimacy) is also the first word of 2435, where it turns into rules of life. பன்றான வாதிகுரு, the many primal gurus, claims a lineage for the teaching.

2435.reading: I will tell more of the secret: in the world do not speak much pointed mockery, do not make enemies, do not speak idly, do not wander the open country, do not climb mountains, do not laugh, do not anger, do not sleep, do not slip and do not fall back from the suzhumunai; knowing the pooranam of the whole world and conquering, become clear and then live in accord with the world.
2435.nuance: The list mixes social rules (no mockery, no enemies) with the yogi's regimen (no laughter, anger or sleep, and no retreat from the suzhumunai), and ends not in withdrawal but in உலகத்தோடு ஒத்து வாழ், living in accord with the world; 2436 then condemns those who leave the world in garb. 'Do not climb mountains' is against the wandering ascetic's life, which 2442 also dismisses.

2436.reading: He who does not live, leaves the world, puts on the garb, talks and talks mouth-knowledge for his belly and begs from every low house is a husk, a chandala who does not know himself, a whole ox; do not listen to the words of such sinners and perish, do not panic, do not be bewildered for the belly; do not listen, do not keep hearing all the talk and be shaken, and do not say 'body and life' as two.
2436.nuance: வாய்ஞானம், mouth-knowledge, is knowledge that is only talk, the opposite of the practice in 2431 to 2433. The verse turns the word சண்டாளர் (outcaste) on the garbed renouncer, as 2413 turned சண்டாளம் on base acts, so that caste language is used against those who claim rank by garb. The last line leads into 2437: body and life are not to be named as separate things.

2437.reading: Body, life and pooranam, the three, are one, though in the world a few people say they are different; if you ask what body, life and pooranam are, noble one, they are the sixteen, the one-four and the eight; body, life and pooranam are Brahma, Vishnu and Isa, and the worldly, not knowing, went bewildered; body and life have become pooranam's foot and head; know the standing of the risen kala and stand in pati.
2437.nuance: The claim is the run's monism: body, life and the fullness are one, mapped onto the three numbers (sixteen, four, eight, from 2432) and the three gods. பூரணடி முடியும், pooranam's foot and head, makes body and life the two ends of one thing. The numbers are cipher and the mapping is tradition's, not explained in the text.

2438.reading: It tells of the guru who is the place where pati is; do not open it in public, your head will split in two; listen as I say what place fate is: it is the uvula within the sky of the sky; moon and sun, pooranam, eye, mouth, nose, the great ear and touch, eight; the place where pati dwells, its name is the suzhumunai; they call it heaven and Kailasa.
2438.nuance: The verse names the place three ways: the uvula within the inner sky, the suzhumunai, and heaven and Kailasa, which 2439 expands into a list of all the holy places. The eight (moon, sun, pooranam and the five senses) is another of the run's counts. விதியின்ன விடம், 'the place where fate is', is strange; a variant sense is 'the place as ordained'. The threat that the head splits in two for telling it openly is a conventional curse on breaking secrecy.

2439.reading: Kailasa, Vaikuntha, the gods' world, Kasi, Kumari and Setu, the cloud where the peacock dances and hell, maya, lightning and silence, the cold wind of sleep, the subtle, the wordless place and the contraction, the oil-smooth foot, foot and head, and the mother substance: these are the names of pati.
2439.nuance: The list makes the pilgrimage sites (Kailasa, Vaikuntha, Kasi, Kanyakumari, Rameswaram), the cosmological places (heaven, hell) and the yogic terms (silence, subtle, wordless, contraction, foot and head) all names of the one inner place of 2438. That the holy places are within the body is a standard Siddhar claim; this verse states it as a bare list of names. காசின்யா for காசி and மயிலாடு மேகம் (the cloud where the peacock dances) are uncertain.

2440.reading: I have told the name, told the town, told the place too; I have told the contraction of the back kala and the front kala; I have told the path of the many books of the wide world; I have told the trade that many people follow; I have told clearly what the glorious world is; I have told in brief all the siddhis that are siddhi; I have told the straight way, the way and the state; I have divided and told what your body is.
2440.nuance: A summary stanza in which every line ends சொன்னேன், 'I have told'. பின்கலையும் முன்கலையும், the back and front kala, are the moon and sun breaths (idakalai and pingalai) in the cipher. 'The trade many follow' is the livelihood religion of 2428 to 2430. The verse claims the run has 'divided the body' (பிரித்துச் சொன்னேன்), that is, given its anatomy as a map of pati.

2441.reading: I have set it out divided within a sutra of twice eight; madmen, if you look and understand it well, I have told the path of the book that was set out at length; do not blurt that this book exists; take it to heart with intent and do not change the kala; hold the matter in mind by thought; I have told in brief all the news the sruti told; I have strung the sixteen like a sutra: complete.
2441.nuance: The run calls itself a sutra of ஈரெட்டு, twice eight, and of பதினாறு, sixteen, which matches its sixteen units and echoes the sixteen kalas it teaches. கலைமாறாதே (do not change the kala) is at once 'do not alter the text' and 'do not let the breath change'. The claim that the run condenses what the sruti said sits in tension with the attack on the Vedas in 2428, unless sruti is here the inner teaching.

links.note: Tirumular says one can guard the four inner instruments, the sixteen kalas and the breath if one stands with the mind fixed; Agasthiyar says that if you set the mind and guard pooranam, which is the sixteen kalas, it becomes the Siva-yoga life called vaasi. Both make guarding the sixteen kalas by a fixed mind the yoga.

Tirumular's sun takes in all sixteen kalas of fulfilment through the great breath; Agasthiyar's sixteen kalas are pooranam, the fullness, kept by the vaasi. The sixteen kalas as the breath's fullness is shared; Agasthiyar makes the number itself the definition of God.

Tirumular says those who set Nandi in love have no caste, no stain and no pride; Agasthiyar says the knowers of pooranam did silent Siva-yoga, and that caste, 'I' and 'you' were set up for the worldly who trust the body. Both place caste among the things the knower is free of; Agasthiyar adds that it was invented for a living.

The Naladiyar says 'good caste' and 'bad caste' are words with nothing behind them, and that austerity, learning and effort make a lineage; Agasthiyar says caste was set up for livelihood. Both deny caste a real basis, the Naladiyar replacing it with merit and Agasthiyar with knowledge of pooranam.

Sivavakkiyar asks what mantra it is to call a planted stone God and circle it muttering, when the Lord is within, and whether the pot that cooked the curry knows its taste; Agasthiyar says the fools who take stone and copper for God, not knowing pooranam, bark like dogs. The same attack on idols, with the same ground, that God is within.

Tirumular says curd, ghee, milk, copper, fire, mercury, brick, bilva or gold can each be the Sivalinga when clearly known; Agasthiyar says those who take stone and copper for God are fools. The conflict holds on the plain reading of both; it softens if Tirumular's 'clearly known' (தெளிந்து) is the knowledge Agasthiyar says the idol-worshippers lack.

Kakapusundar says that when the mind is driven straight to the uvula it leaps to the suzhumunai and the five elements become one; Agasthiyar says that when the mind is set at the suzhumunai and guarded as one thought, the four and the eight become one. Both make the mind's fixing at the central channel the point where the many become one.

The Thirumular Njanam says the two lights rise and subside in the root of the supreme Siva, and the suzhumunai becomes the pillar and the light that is truth; Agasthiyar says the sun and moon exchange and rise at the suzhumunai and subside within it. The same picture of the two breaths meeting and sinking at the central channel.

Tirumular says the false garb is worn for the sake of eating and only the knower's garb saves; Agasthiyar says he who puts on the garb and talks mouth-knowledge for his belly, begging at every house, is a husk who does not know himself. Both tie the false ascetic's garb to the belly.

Pattinathar addresses pooranam as the one who rose as the left, right and central channels and stood as body and life; Agasthiyar says body, life and pooranam are one, body and life being its foot and head. Both speak of pooranam as that which is the body and the life, not something beyond them.

Tirumular's teacher set the thing to meditate on daily below the crown and above the uvula, with the mouth not opened; Agasthiyar's pati dwells in the uvula within the inner sky, and the place is not to be opened in public. The same body-place and the same secrecy; Agasthiyar names it the suzhumunai and Kailasa.

Tirumular says the Lord is not in the mansion, hall, courtyard, temple or holy garb but in the hidden place in the heart of those who have given up longing; Agasthiyar makes Kailasa, Vaikuntha, Kasi, Kumari and Setu names of the inner place of pati. Both relocate the holy place within; Agasthiyar does it by renaming the pilgrimage sites rather than denying them.

new_concepts.gloss: fullness: the whole that the Siddhars call God, defined by Agasthiyar as the sixteen kalas kept whole in the breath, and said to be one with body and life
new_concepts.label_source: The verses use the word in nearly every stanza (2426, 2427, 2428, 2429, 2430, 2432, 2434, 2435, 2437, 2438), and 2426 defines it.

new_concepts.gloss: the breath as the Siddhars' practice: the vital air raised, held and reversed along the central channel (also the 'horse' of their cipher), and the Siva-yoga built on it
new_concepts.label_source: 2426 names the practice வாசியென்ற சிவயோக வாழ்க்கை and 2427 places the keepers of pooranam வாசிநடு மையத்துள், in the centre of the vaasi.

new_concepts.gloss: the central channel of the yogic body (sushumna), between the left and right breath channels, where the Siddhars set the mind and where the two breaths meet; also the place at the brow or uvula where it is felt
new_concepts.label_source: The verses use the word (2431, 2433 twice, 2435, 2438), and 2438 says it is the name of the place where pati dwells.

new_concepts.gloss: the Siddhars' cipher: the coded vocabulary (sun and moon, horse, serpent, numbers, salt, elephant) in which their books are written, so that they can be read only by one who holds the key
new_concepts.label_source: 2430 uses the Tamil form பரிபாடை (the fools do not know the cipher); the Sanskrit-derived form பரிபாஷை is the word elsewhere in the corpus (Kakapusundar).

source_issues: 2429 has உழைப்பதற்கு at the start of both line 3 and line 7; one is probably a copyist's repetition (பிழைப்பதற்கு or தழைப்பதற்கு may be meant).
2432 line 3 வாதிகளே (disputants) as a vocative is odd and may be corrupt for a word in -ளே addressing the disciple.
2439 line 2 காசின்யா (for காசி) and line 3 மயிலாடு மேகம் are doubtful readings.
2441 calls the run a sutra of twice eight and of sixteen; the run has sixteen units, so the count is consistent and no unit is missing.
